title: A 7.8km Line Older Than the Forbidden City — Beijing Central Axis EP1 | China Travel Expert
description:
New route series: walking Beijing's Central Axis, stop by stop. First, the line the whole city is built around.

Beijing's Central Axis is a 7.8 km north-south line running from Yongdingmen Gate in the south to the Bell & Drum Towers in the north, with the Forbidden City sitting right on it. It was laid out in the Yuan dynasty in the 13th century — so it predates and anchors the Forbidden City (built 1406-1420). In July 2024 UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage Site: fifteen monuments threaded on one straight line, 'a building ensemble exhibiting the ideal order of the Chinese capital.'

🧭 Expert Tip: For the single best view of the whole axis, climb Jingshan hill just north of the Forbidden City — from Wanchun Pavilion you look straight down the line over the palace roofs to the Bell & Drum Towers. To walk it, start south at Yongdingmen and head north.

北京7.8公里的中轴线，比故宫还早，整座城依它而建。
